args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-round-half-even
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
`src/money.py`'s docstring said it used banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but the code actually called `ROUND_HALF_UP`. Because of that, `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` failed (2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66) and the nightly build broke.

This PR switches `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the nightly build failure, CI passed, and the pull request is open with alex as reviewer.

- **Cause:** `src/money.py` says in its comment that it uses banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212), but the code actually rounded `.5` up. So 2.665 came out as 2.67 instead of the 2.66 the test expects.
- **Fix:** On a new branch, `fix/money-round-half-even`, I changed `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. That was the only change.
- **CI:** The run on that branch (ci-0001) passed.
- **Pull request:** #101 against main: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

I tried to look up FIN-212 to check the requirement, but the lookup tool didn't recognise that ID. The fix is based on what the test expects and what the code comment says. I haven't merged it, because merging into main needs a code owner's approval.
